contents.name: Definition 7.1: f-divergence and its recession boundary term
contents.support: The source defines the generator integral and adds the singular mass through its recession derivative. The local finite definition states the corresponding finite sum and proves existence of the extended generator limits in lem-convex-generator-boundary-limits-exist.

contents.name: Remark 7.1: discrete probability-mass-function form
contents.support: This gives the discrete coordinate formula used by the local finite-alphabet definition, including its zero-coordinate convention.

contents.name: Theorem 7.3 (Monotonicity), with complete proof
contents.support: The full conditional-Jensen proof handles general measures and singular terms. The assigned theorem gives a self-contained finite-kernel proof via the closed perspective lemma, so the source argument is supporting context rather than an imported proof.

contents.name: Theorem 7.4 (Data processing) for a common channel
contents.support: The channel applies the same conditional law to both input laws and contracts every f-divergence, matching the local stochastic-kernel statement.

contents.name: Definition 7.22: positive-order Rényi divergence
contents.support: The local affinity formula is the finite-alphabet specialization; its support cases are stated directly and checked in the disjoint-support example.

contents.name: Definition 14.1: Neyman–Pearson region and lower boundary
contents.support: Its null-acceptance constraint at level gamma is exactly the local rejection constraint epsilon after setting gamma=1−epsilon; the local definition states both hypotheses and error orientation explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 14.10 (Neyman–Pearson likelihood-ratio rule), with complete proof
contents.support: The book proves the general randomized likelihood-ratio boundary rule. The binary example verifies its own candidate and optimality by a direct two-case calculation, with alternative-to-null ratio q/p stated explicitly.

contents.name: Theorem 14.13 (Stein’s lemma), with complete proof
contents.support: The source states the iid exponent for fixed null-acceptance probability; the local theorem sets that probability to 1−epsilon and proves the exact finite-alphabet limit, including P not absolutely continuous with respect to Q.

contents.name: Definition 2 (Simple Orders): Rényi formula and zero/support conventions

contents.name: Theorem 5 and its complete proof: order-one identity and continuity caveat
contents.support: The source proves the left limit and gives a condition for right continuity, while documenting that right continuity can fail in general spaces. The local finite proof establishes both one-sided limits directly and treats support mismatch separately.

contents.name: Theorem 9 (Data Processing Inequality) and proof for extended orders
contents.support: The source transfers simple-order data processing to extended orders. The local theorem separately derives every finite order alpha>0, alpha≠1, from the f-divergence contraction and the appropriate monotone transform.

contents.support: The source explicitly relates the zero extension to the recession limit and writes the singular contribution when absolute continuity fails. The local item proves the finite generator limits and records the finite-alphabet coordinate convention.

contents.name: Equations (41)–(45): relative entropy as an f-divergence
contents.support: The paper identifies t log t and its affine-equivalent normalized generator for relative entropy. The local KL definition uses t log t and the KL-generator lemma verifies convexity and both boundary values directly.

contents.support: The introduction records data processing as a standard property but does not provide its proof in the inspected definition range. No proof is harvested from this statement; the finite contraction proof is supplied locally.

The local definition specializes these conventions to finite vectors, states both error sums, and explicitly orients P as null and Q as alternative.
